blocks.text: Declension of masculine and neuter nouns (singular)
Note. The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.

Peculiarities. a) Certain masculine nouns have the vowels е or о only in the nominative singular (and in the accusative if inanimate): отец — отца, американец — американца, кусок — куска, звонок — звонка. e) Russian masculine surnames in -ов, -ев, -ин take the ending -ым in the instrumental: с господином Ивановым, с Гусевым, с Рудиным.

Note. The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю. There are some masculine nouns ending in -а, -я which are declined like feminine nouns: мужчина, старшина, дедушка, дядя. The modifiers of these nouns remain in masculine forms: *Мой старый дедушка.*

Russian feminine surnames in -ова, -ева, -ина have the usual ending -у in the accusative; in other cases they take the ending -ой: госпожа Иванова, госпожи Ивановой, госпоже Ивановой, госпожу Иванову, госпожой Ивановой, о госпоже Ивановой. Other Russian or foreign surnames, when referred to women, are never declined: *Я знаю господина Смита.* but: *Я знаю госпожу Смит.*
